findings.text: finish() labels EVERY failed job with hardcoded t.ErrorKey="MessageTaskCanceledByUser"; upstream sets that key only in cancelEncode and uses distinct keys for real failures (target not writable, metadata write failed) — ffmpeg/process failures surface to admins as 'Task canceled by user'. Misleading, divergent from the pinned oracle.

Long-running ffmpeg jobs never emit track_started/track_progress/task_progress, which upstream's merge path emits per track and contracts/source-inventory.json lists as expected events — only track_finished and task_started/finished exist; admin progress monitoring silently unfinished.

sha1-ETag writeStatus/writeExpressText/writeExpressSend and the JSON write() helpers are byte-identical duplicated copies in both packages while internal/identity already owns the Express-shape writer; admin() and librariesAccessible checks are triplicated reimplementations with a clear owner (httputil/leaf permission helper).

device["email"].(string) unchecked type-assertion on DB-stored JSON: the endpoint only validates jsTruthy(name/email), so a device stored with a non-string email passes validation and then panics sendEbook — net/http merely drops the connection with no error surfaced; should be a comma-ok assertion/500.
'from, _ := m["fromAddress"]; _ = from' dead variable + dead assignment; the from address is actually read again inside sendMail.
AddTestClient test-only hook (nil socket clients with testEmit observer) lives in production hub code Emit iterates on every broadcast; documented and gated, but a test seam in the hot path.

All three packages use hand-rolled Handle(...) bool chains with manual path splitting instead of http.ServeMux patterns + typed DTOs (consistent with the 13 ratchet-baselined routers, but violates the stated structure rule).

deliverActive unconditionally saves and broadcasts notifications_updated on every fire attempt even when nothing but counters changed; testEvent discards the delivery result and always returns 200 — mirrors upstream semantics but extra write traffic.
